messages:
Ajay: Hey team — new artifact arrived from partner, want to kick off intake + quick bring-up. Files at s3://partner-drop/orchid-3b/ (pytorch_model.bin, tokenizer.json, signature.asc). Can we run provenance + a minimal quant/bench plan? What priority should this get? :thinking:

Sasha: Quick thoughts: verify checksums, verify signature, copy to registry staging, add metadata YAML, then smoke latency + basic quality. If license is CC-BY-NC we need legal review before public catalog.

Ajay: Good call on license. Partner said non-commercial, so add hold until legal confirms. Meanwhile can ops snag the artifacts for staging?

ingest-bot: Automated scan: s3://partner-drop/orchid-3b/ - no public ACLs, size total 12.3GB, objects: 3. Created 2026-03-15T09:12:02Z. Checksums missing on source. Tagging with ingest:pending.

Maria_G: I'll grab a staging copy and run checksum/signature verify. Plan: 1) cp to /tmp, 2) sha256sum, 3) gpg verify, 4) push to registry with metadata. Rough commands:```bash
aws s3 cp s3://partner-drop/orchid-3b/ /tmp/orchid-3b --recursive
sha256sum /tmp/orchid-3b/* > /tmp/orchid-3b/checksums.txt
gpg --verify /tmp/orchid-3b/signature.asc /tmp/orchid-3b/pytorch_model.bin
```

Kyle: Add to that: record the signing key fingerprint in metadata and store signed checksums in KMS-backed ledger. Registry path suggestion: s3://redwood-model-registry/staging/orchid-3b/2026-03-15/. Metadata fields: name, version, source_url, source_commit, license, signer_fingerprint, sha256_checksums, ingest_ticket. Example YAML snippet:```yaml
name: orchid-3b
version: 0.1.0
source: s3://partner-drop/orchid-3b/
license: CC-BY-NC
signer_fingerprint: "AB12 34CD ..."
sha256: "<link-to-checksums>"
registered_by: Maria_G
```

Sasha: For bring-up/quant plan (minimal): - smoke int8 quant (static) and fp16 baseline - run bench-runner v2 on 100-sample latency set - run small eval suite (50 prompts) for BERTScore/ROUGE to catch egregious regressions - expected goals: int8 <= 0.8x tokens/sec slowdown vs fp16? actually target latency < 70% of fp16, cost reduction > 2x.

Ajay: Can you outline commands for tokenizer sanity? Want to ensure tokenization parity with partner claims.

Maria_G: Tokenizer quick test:```bash
python - <<PY
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
t = Tokenizer.from_file('/tmp/orchid-3b/tokenizer.json')
print(t.encode('Hello, world!').tokens)
PY
```Also run vocab consistency: check size, unk id, BOS/EOS tokens. If partner included vocab.txt confirm mapping.

Kyle: Quant experiments: We should follow standard experiment matrix: static post-training quant (calibration set size 512), dynamic quant, and LLM.int8() path used by runtime. Label experiments: q_static_512, q_dynamic, q_llmint8. Use bench runner:```bash
bench-runner --model /tmp/orchid-3b/pytorch_model.bin --tokenizer /tmp/orchid-3b/tokenizer.json --mode latency --batch 1 --dataset eval/latency_100.json --out results/latency.json
```
Save outputs per run to s3://redwood-model-results/orchid-3b/<experiment>/

Sasha: Important: attach eval prompts + expected golden outputs for regression detection. We'll run the Redwood eval harness with thresholds and auto-alert on >5% BERTScore drop vs baseline. Also capture generation artifacts for human spot-check.

Ajay: Priority — since partner is a strategic channel partner but license is restrictive -> mark as "medium" until legal clears, but queue quant experiments in non-public staging so we can estimate cost/latency. Maria, can you start checks now and tag ticket #ENGML-872?

Maria_G: Starting now. Will post checksum + signature verification in the thread when done. Tagging ticket ENGML-872. ETA for smoke bench: ~4 hours (includes staging copy + quant run).

ingest-bot: Copy to registry staging started by Maria_G at 2026-03-15T09:22:10Z. Upload progress reported.

Sasha: Also: if we see tokenizer mismatch (special tokens diff) don't proceed with quant until partner confirms mapping. Tokenizer mismatches cause big quality regressions.

Kyle: Ops note: when pushing to registry set ACL private, enable server-side encryption (SSE-KMS), and add tag team=eng-ml, sensitivity=partner-prop. Also create a registry record in our DB with ingest_state: pending_verification.

Maria_G: Done with checksums and signature. Output: sha256sum file uploaded to s3://redwood-model-registry/staging/orchid-3b/2026-03-15/checksums.txt; gpg verify OK, signer fingerprint AB12:34CD:56EF. Uploaded model to staging path with tags. Pushing metadata YAML now.

Ajay: Awesome. Once legal confirms license we'll decide publish vs private only. Sasha/Kyle — after smoke runs, if int8 quality delta < 2% BERTScore drop, consider promoting a quant profile to dedicated pool for cost testing.

Sasha: Ack. Plan for human QA sampling after automated checks. Will allocate 10 reviews from review pool.

Maria_G: Smoke bench results (first pass): fp16 median latency 120ms, int8_static_512 95ms. BERTScore delta ~1.8% vs fp16 on 50-sample eval. Uploading full logs to s3://redwood-model-results/orchid-3b/initial-smoke/.

Kyle: Those numbers look promising. Next: run longer perf run (1k prompts) and measure memory/throughput before any rollout. I'll reserve a quant-slot tonight.

Ajay: Thanks all. Leaving this thread open. Please post final ingest ticket update and next steps once legal gives license OK. :white_check_mark:
